sentences.text: 1. The claimant is in appeal challenging the judgment and award of the Tribunal on the ground of quantum of compensation as well as negligence.

2. As far as negligence is concerned, it is noticed that admittedly, the charge sheet was laid against the driver of the tipper lorry and evidence on record indicates that the driver of the lorry was pleaded guilty before the criminal court.
The driver of the lorry, who was examined has stated that he was not driving the vehicle and he appeared before the criminal court only because the owner of the lorry asked him to plead guilty.
There is thus absolutely no direct evidence to prove the manner in which the accident occurred.

3. The learned counsel for the insurer contends that the ARTO, who was examined has stated that the accident had occurred only because three people were traveling on the motorcycle and this statement is made on the basis of the damage caused to the motorcycle.
It is also his contention that since two wheeler hit the tipper lorry, certain negligence has to be attributed to the rider of the motorcycle, especially when three people were riding the motorcycle.

4. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of MOHAMMED SIDDIQUE AND ANOTHER -V- NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LTD AND OTHERS (AIR 2020 SC 520), has held that mere traveling of three people in the motorcycle cannot lead to assumption that was the cause of accident.

entities.text: MOHAMMED SIDDIQUE AND ANOTHER -V- NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LTD AND OTHERS (AIR 2020 SC 520)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to attribute negligence, there must be positive evidence to prove that the rider of the motorcycle was negligent and he had contributed to the accident.
In this case, there is no positive evidence indicating that the rider of the motorcycle had contributed to the accident.

5. In the light of the fact that the driver of the lorry pleaded guilty before the criminal court,
attribution of negligence to the extent of 30% on the claimant cannot be sustained and hence the finding of the Tribunal in so far as negligence is concerned, the same is set side.

sentences.text:
As far as quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence, has recorded a finding that the claimant has suffered closed comminuted supracondular fracture right distal femur, subtrochantric fracture right femur, closed comminuted right zygomatic arch fracture,
right facial palsy.

7. The doctor, who was examined has stated that claimant cannot walk independently, and needed support of walker and there is limb disability of 71% and on reunion, the whole body disability is likely to be 22%.
The Tribunal has concluded that the claimant has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 17% to the whole body, which is incorrect.
Having regard to the nature of injuries and evidence of doctor, in my view, it would be appropriate to determine the whole body disability at 22%.
8. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.6,000/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which, for the accident of the year 2015, would be Rs.9,000/-.
9.
As the claimant was aged 26 years, a multiplier of '17' would have to be applied.
Since the whole body disability is determined at 22%, the claimant is entitled for addition of 40% of the income towards future prospects, which would be Rs.12,600/- (9,000+40%).
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.565,488/- (12,600 x 12 x 17 x 22%) towards 'loss of future income' .
10. The Tribunal has not awarded any compensation for 'loss of income during laid-up period'.

Hence, in my view, considering the laid up period as 3 months, a sum of Rs.27,000/- (9000 x 3 months) is awarded towards 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
11.
Having regard to the injuries suffered by the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' as against Rs.45,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

12. Having regard to the lasting effects of the injuries on the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards loss of amenities, as against the sum of Rs.25,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

13. Having regard to the nature of injuries, length of the stay of the claimant in the hospital and medical bills produced by the claimant, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards 'conveyance, food and nourishment and attendant charges', 'medical expenses' and 'future medical expenses' are just and proper.
14. Consequently the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:

The Tribunal after deducting 30% negligence on the part of the claimant has awarded compensation of Rs.3,90,737/-.
16.

Since this court has set aside the finding of the Tribunal regarding negligence and held that the driver of the tipper lorry alone is negligent in causing the accident, the claimant is entitled to the total compensation of Rs.10,83,803/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
17.

18. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
19. The disbursement of the compensation amount shall be in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
